files.reason: Admission and validation code, runtime-generated templates, historical paths/hashes, model/settings constants and aggregate constraints. Scientific profiles/items/requests and control records are loaded through variables; no actual scientific body, issued private control document or credential literal was found embedded.

Diagnostic wrapper with historical path/hash constants, request digest strings and generic status/error identifiers. Runtime events, responses and control records are read or generated dynamically; no actual private event/response/error body or credential literal was found embedded.

Terminal verification and accounting logic containing schemas, counts and metadata checks. Actual packets, profile/release bodies, predictions and ledger rows are variable-loaded rather than literal copies.

Launcher containing pinned source/envelope references and a credential-file path. The credential path and parsing call are code references, with no actual credential value embedded. Eligibility is not permission to launch it.

Control tests with synthetic authority/envelope mutations and metadata expectations. Some test paths would load real referenced inputs if executed; those inputs are not embedded, and neither tests nor references were executed or followed.
Admission test code with helper/path references, metadata expectations and mocks. Actual draft/profile data would be obtained at runtime and are not embedded in the submitted source.

Wrapper test code with helper paths, source/hash metadata and AST comparison logic. Referenced helper bodies were not followed or copied; no actual private scientific data or credentials were embedded.

Synthetic terminal-row and accounting fixtures, generic generated item/target/donor markers, mutations and assertions. Fixture bodies are visibly constructed test scaffolding rather than copied actual scientific predictions or labels.

Independent test code with explicitly mocked HTTP output, request identifiers, synthetic credential marker and generated authority fixture. Actual profile/release inputs are runtime-loaded; no actual private scientific body, credential or issued private control document was found embedded. Tests were not executed.

Seven-packet preparation code with source/control references, model/settings constants, aggregate accounting constraints and dynamic request construction. Profiles, target items, responses, ledger rows and issued control records are not embedded as actual bodies.

limits: This is a bounded source publication eligibility review, not a comprehensive security audit, correctness review, portability check, scientific validation, or authorization to run code.
Historical machine paths, source/config hashes, model names and variable names are references, not proof of dependency retention or content truth.

Synthetic credential/response/authority fixtures were distinguished from actual credentials, scientific payloads or copied private control documents. Tests that dynamically load actual artifacts were not treated as wholly synthetic execution.

No embedded paths, imports, review references, dynamic inputs or other dependency references were followed; no referenced profile, prompt, target/label, prediction, response, error, control, environment or database body was opened.
No submitted source bodies or excerpts were copied into these artifacts. Only newly authored metadata, notes and the identity checker are retained.
Decision applies only to the ten exact hashes and sizes listed here. It does not extend to indices 10-19, future edits, referenced inputs, execution, or final publication authority.
method: Every line of each of the ten exact source texts was inspected statically, including comments and literal strings.
Regular nonsymlink path verification used no-follow directory and file descriptors; exact hashes, sizes and file states matched before/after the initial reads and at the final recheck.
AST parsing and auxiliary literal-shape screening were inspection aids only; no submitted module or test was imported or executed.
The final source display for index 9 was split into lines 1-35, 36-68 and 69-97 after a whole-file display was truncated; all 97 lines were then inspected.
